note: Two shape sets in one topology. Statehood (groups orig, e1821, e1859, e1896, e1959): today's state shapes, valid from the day each state ratified the Constitution (the original 13) or was admitted (Newberry START_DATE of the first state version; checked against the US Statutes dates). Civil War (groups cw_*): every state and territory version valid 6 Nov 1860 - 15 Jul 1870, split at the date of each state's ordinance of secession and of its readmission to representation in Congress. Dates in the build script's events file (tools/build/us_history_events.json) with their sources.

items.title: South Carolina secedes
items.text: Six weeks after Abraham Lincoln won the presidential election, a convention in South Carolina voted to leave the Union. Six more states of the Deep South followed by 1 February 1861.

items.title: The Confederacy is formed
items.text: Delegates of the seven seceded states formed the Confederate States of America at Montgomery, Alabama. Historians widely agree that preserving slavery was its principal aim.

items.title: Fort Sumter
items.text: Confederate forces fired on the federal fort in Charleston harbour, and the war began. Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina and Tennessee seceded in the following eight weeks.

items.title: Emancipation Proclamation
items.text: Lincoln declared enslaved people in the areas still in rebellion to be free. It did not cover the slave states that had stayed in the Union.

items.title: West Virginia
items.text: The north-western counties of Virginia, which had rejected secession, were admitted as the new state of West Virginia.
items.source: Newberry Library AHCB; Wikipedia, 'Confederate States of America'

items.title: Gettysburg and Vicksburg
items.text: In the first days of July 1863 the Union army turned back Lee's invasion of the North at Gettysburg, and Vicksburg on the Mississippi surrendered on 4 July.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Battle of Gettysburg' and 'Siege of Vicksburg'

items.title: Surrender at Appomattox
items.text: General Robert E. Lee surrendered his army at Appomattox Court House. Most other Confederate forces surrendered by May 1865.

items.title: Slavery abolished
items.text: The Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, abolishing slavery everywhere in the United States, was ratified.

items.title: Georgia readmitted
items.text: Georgia was the last former Confederate state readmitted; its representatives took their seats in Congress in February 1871.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Confederate States of America' and 'Reconstruction era'
